- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.30) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak or 1.5% below 30d moving average.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon (first 5–7 days) — add 0.8–1.2% to initial forecast values.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays reaction — forecast should accelerate upward by 0.3–0.7% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by downward correction, reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30d MA by >2%, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from -0.4 to +0.2) triggers lagged reaction — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and scale down magnitude by 0.5–0.8.
